LTRAC-1859: docs(skills) - Fix the integration-branch sync docs (#3220)

* LTRAC-1859: docs(skills) - Correct the b2b-makeswift sync reference

Three claims in the reference were wrong at the 1.11.1 release and sent
the sync down the wrong path.

The catch-up note said b2b trails makeswift "by several minors" and
directed a tag-by-tag merge of @1.7.0 through @1.9.0. It has not been
true for some time: the merge base was makeswift's immediately preceding
release, b2b was missing only the current release's commits, and both
branches sat at the same version. Replaced with the steady-state
description, plus an instruction to verify rather than trust the note,
since this is what went stale last time.

Two surface paths predate canary's middlewares/ to proxies/ rename:
core/middlewares/with-b2b.ts is core/proxies/with-b2b.ts, and the
withB2B wiring lives in core/proxy.ts, not core/middleware.ts. A sync
checking the surface against the old paths finds nothing and cannot tell
that apart from a clobbered surface.

The remaining entries were correct but vague enough to be unverifiable,
so the register route, the quote vibes components, the B2BLoader layout,
and the en.json keys are now named explicitly. The layout entry also
claimed a glob of files; only core/app/[locale]/layout.tsx references
B2BLoader.

Refs LTRAC-1859
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* LTRAC-1859: docs(skills) - Explain unrelated-histories on a shallow clone

Phase 1 of the b2b sync during the 1.11.1 release died with `refusing to
merge unrelated histories`, which reads as the merge base having been
destroyed -- the exact failure the skill's do-not-squash warnings exist to
prevent. It was only a shallow clone, which contains no common ancestor to
find.

The two corroborating symptoms are recorded alongside it, because they are
just as alarming and just as benign: `git merge-base` exits non-zero with
no output, and `git rev-list --max-parents=0` reports recent commits as
roots. Diagnosing this from scratch costs real time when the obvious
reading is that an integration branch has been ruined.

Also warns off `--allow-unrelated-histories`, which is the tempting next
move and would fabricate a merge across histories git cannot see the join
of.

Refs LTRAC-1859

LTRAC-1883: fix(core) - Stop sending X-Correlation-ID on cacheable requests (#3221)

The correlation ID is a fresh UUID per request, and Next.js includes request
headers in its Data Cache key. Every fetch configured with `next: { revalidate }`
therefore computed a unique key on every request: it always missed, always went
out to the BigCommerce GraphQL API, and always wrote an entry nothing would ever
read again. On a product page that is ~12 queries paying full uncached cost on
every page view, plus unbounded growth in the data cache.

Attach the header only when `fetchOptions.cache` is `no-store` or `no-cache`,
matching the rule already applied to `X-Forwarded-For` and `True-Client-IP` in
the same hook. Those requests are uncacheable by construction, so there is no
cache key to pollute, and they are the per-customer requests where a correlation
ID is most useful for tracing.

Drop the surrounding try/catch: it guarded against `React.cache` being
unavailable during next.config.ts resolution, but that path passes no
fetchOptions and so no longer reaches the import.

Fixes LTRAC-1883

TRAC-969: Create reusable preview deployment action (#3194)

* TRAC-969: feat(deployment-preview-action) - Add pull request preview deployments

Native hosting gives a project one hostname, not one per deployment, so pull
request previews have to share a single project and take turns. The newest open
pull request deploys automatically; any other claims the preview by commenting
`redeploy preview`, and the one that held it gets a notice in place of its old
comment.

Displacing a pull request costs one listing call rather than one per open pull
request: open pull requests are walked newest-activity-first and the search
stops at the first one holding a preview, because only one ever does.

The action shells out to the consuming project's own Catalyst CLI, so the CLI
version stays the merchant's choice, and talks to GitHub with plain fetch rather
than a bundled client -- three calls do not justify a dependency, and an action
shipped without node_modules is one less thing to keep patched.

Most consumers should call the reusable workflow, which owns the concurrency
group: every preview shares one hosting project, and two deploys at once would
race for it. A workflow in core/ means a scaffolded storefront starts with
previews wired up, inert until a project UUID is configured, so a new storefront
does not get a red X on its first pull request for a feature it never opted
into.

Nothing compiles action.yml, so the tests parse it, syntax-check every run block
and pin the couplings that have already broken once: an empty env block the
runner rejects, a check row named after a job, and README claims that drifted
from the comments the code posts.

Refs TRAC-969
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* TRAC-969: ci(changesets) - Release the preview action on moving major tags

The action versions through changesets like every other package here, but a
consumer references it by git ref, and a changesets tag contains an `@`, which
cannot be used in a `uses:` line. Tag each release as preview-action-v<version>
and move preview-action-v<major> to it, so `@preview-action-v1` keeps working
and picks up fixes.

Refs TRAC-969
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

LTRAC-1807: fix(cli) - Stop `upgrade` reverting the CLI-managed npm scripts (#3225)

`catalyst create` points `build`/`start`/`deploy` at the CLI so they dispatch
on project state, but the upstream tree keeps its own `next`-based commands.
Those lines were therefore a permanent ours-vs-base difference that `upgrade`
did nothing about, and core 1.11.0 added `"test": "vitest run"` directly below
`"start"` — putting a real upstream insertion next to the one line the CLI had
rewritten. Neither merge engine could reconcile them, so `package.json` came
out conflicted, and resolving toward the incoming side silently reverted
`catalyst start` to `next start`.

Pin both downloaded sides to the commands the project already has for those
keys before merging, so the merge sees no change there and additions around
them still apply cleanly. Only keys the project has diverged from its base on
are pinned, which leaves a genuine upstream edit free to come through. Where
the two versions do disagree about one of these scripts — changed, introduced
or dropped — the upgrade reports it instead of hiding it behind the pin.

Fixes LTRAC-1807

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

LTRAC-1721: fix(cli) - Re-authenticate an expired token without a logout first (#3226)

Every authenticated command answers a rejected token by telling the user to
run `catalyst auth login`, but login only checked whether credentials were
present, not whether they still worked — so it replied "Already logged in ...
run `catalyst auth logout` first". The two commands sent the user in a circle
with no way out but knowing to log out by hand.

Login now verifies the credentials it finds before refusing. Still-valid ones
behave as before; rejected ones fall through to re-authentication. A failure
that isn't a rejection (API unreachable, 5xx) counts as "couldn't tell" and
keeps the credentials, since the device-code flow needs the same network that
just failed.

Passing --store-hash and --access-token now stores them, which is what the
help text has always claimed. That path previously reported "Already logged
in" and exited without writing anything, leaving the next command just as
unauthenticated. Rejected credentials are reported rather than silently
swapped for a browser login; unverifiable ones are stored with a warning.

Also adds --force to skip verification and re-authenticate outright.

Fixes LTRAC-1721

  existing @bigcommerce/catalyst-b2b-makeswift@latest git tag.

  changeset:version, headline resolution), trigger it on integrations/b2b-makeswift,
  and map that branch to @bigcommerce/catalyst-b2b-makeswift.
- Retarget the prevent-invalid-changesets guard to integrations/b2b-makeswift and
  @bigcommerce/catalyst-b2b-makeswift.
- Add the changeset:version script and sync-catalyst-version.mts so core's
  catalyst field (version + ref) stays synced on release.
- Update CONTRIBUTING.md package-identity rules to the b2b-makeswift name.

Refs TRAC-1235

* Toast notification now appears when an item is added.
* Cart button badge updates to “1” when the first product is added.

Cause
-----
React 18 / Next.js bug remounts a memoised client component rendered
directly by an RSC, wiping its state

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/44901
https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/73507

Fix
---
Introduce `MakeswiftComponentShim`, a non-memo wrapper around
`MakeswiftComponent`, which prevents the unwanted remount.

Cleanup
-------
Remove the shim once the upstream bug is resolved.

LTRAC-1946: fix(cli) - Correct the managed-zone checkout URL advice (#3240)

* LTRAC-1946: fix(cli) - Correct the managed-zone checkout URL advice

The cross-domain checkout diagnostic told merchants that a storefront on an
auto-generated deployment hostname could never have a checkout URL, because a
checkout subdomain of one "cannot be issued a certificate", and pointed them at
`catalyst domains add` to buy a custom domain instead.

That reasoning is wrong. The auto-generated hostnames are Cloudflare for SaaS
custom hostnames rather than names covered by a single-level wildcard
certificate, and custom hostnames have no label-depth limit — each is issued its
own certificate. The harm was sending merchants to acquire a domain they do not
need.

The diagnostic now names the checkout hostname that will exist and reports it as
not provisioned yet, and no longer recommends adding a custom domain.

`suggestCheckoutUrl` gains a managed-zone mode. It prefixed `checkout.`
unconditionally, naming a hostname nobody will create on a managed zone and
spending nine characters of a 64-character certificate common-name budget the
project name has to share.

Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: a checkout URL is still neither offered nor
suggested on a managed zone, since the hostname is not provisioned yet. Correct
the two comments that justified that guard with the same wrong premise — the
guard matters more than they implied, because BigCommerce would accept such a
URL and leave checkout resolving without a certificate.

Fixes LTRAC-1946
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* LTRAC-1946: fix(cli) - Print the command that provisions the checkout hostname

The managed-zone diagnostic said the checkout hostname "isn't provisioned
yet", as if something else would create it later. Testing on integration
showed the checkout-url PUT is itself what provisions it: BigCommerce
registers the hostname with bcserver, which creates the Cloudflare custom
hostname and issues its certificate.

The diagnostic now names the hostname and prints the exact
`channels update --checkout-url` command that sets it. The guards that skip
the generic advice on a managed zone stay; their comments now give the real
reason.

Managed-zone detection now uses the zones native hosting generates
hostnames under, mirroring ignition's reserved suffix list. Deriving zones
from `deployment_hostnames` counted merchant domains added with
`catalyst domains add`, which appear there too, so a merchant's own domain
could be called an auto-generated hostname. The check is now synchronous,
so the "zone unknown" fallback and the projects lookup go away.

Refs LTRAC-1946

LTRAC-1962: feat(cli) - Put checkout on the storefront's domain for native hosting (#3248)

Setting a channel's checkout URL to c.<project>.<zone> provisions that
hostname (DNS, Cloudflare custom hostname and certificate), so the CLI writes
it first and then waits for the certificate, removing the URL again if none
issues. An interactive deploy now offers to point the channel's site URL at
the deployment and to move checkout onto the c. hostname; both default to No,
declines are saved per channel in project.json, and nothing is asked without
a TTY or with CI set. `channels update` offers the checkout move after a site
URL change.

Previously landed as #3243 on the LTRAC-1946 branch, which was then
force-pushed without it; this reapplies the same change on canary.

Refs LTRAC-1962, LTRAC-2014

Cause
-----
React 18 / Next.js bug remounts a memoised client component rendered
directly by an RSC, wiping its state

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/44901
https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/73507

Fix
---
Introduce `MakeswiftComponentShim`, a non-memo wrapper around
`MakeswiftComponent`, which prevents the unwanted remount.

Cleanup
-------
Remove the shim once the upstream bug is resolved.
